summary: The study investigates the influence of ozone concentration during atomic layer deposition (ALD) of HfO2 films on their dielectric properties and interface trap density (Dit). The research focuses on how varying O3 concentrations affect the performance of HfO2 gate dielectrics on Si substrates, particularly in terms of leakage current, capacitance-equivalent-thickness (CET), and interface states. The results show that higher O3 concentrations lead to increased interface trap density and degradation in dielectric performance, especially at elevated post-deposition annealing (PDA) temperatures.
